quests.sentence: Our students grades improved after the new tutoring program
quests.correctAnswer: Our students' grades improved after the new tutoring program.
quests.hint: More than one student is involved — where does the apostrophe go on a plural noun that already ends in 's'?
quests.explanation: For a plural noun ending in 's,' add only an apostrophe after the 's' to show possession.

quests.sentence: Our gym offers three group classes yoga spinning and boxing
quests.correctAnswer: Our gym offers three group classes: yoga, spinning, and boxing.
quests.hint: A complete sentence is about to introduce a list — what mark sets up the list?
quests.explanation: A colon can follow a complete sentence to introduce a list of items.

quests.sentence: The rain finally stopped the streets were still flooded
quests.correctAnswer: The rain finally stopped; the streets were still flooded.
quests.hint: Two related but separate ideas sit side by side — what links them without a conjunction?
quests.explanation: A semicolon can join two closely related independent clauses when no connecting word is used.

quests.sentence: Thank you Maria for staying late to finish the project
quests.correctAnswer: Thank you, Maria, for staying late to finish the project.
quests.hint: Maria is being spoken to directly — set her name off from the rest of the sentence.
quests.explanation: When addressing someone directly by name, commas separate the name from the rest of the sentence.

quests.sentence: Our childrens playground needs new equipment

quests.hint: 'Children' is already plural — how do you show that the playground belongs to them?
quests.explanation: 'Children' is an irregular plural, so possession is shown by adding an apostrophe and 's,' just like a singular noun.

quests.sentence: There was only one problem with the plan nobody had a car

quests.hint: A complete sentence is about to explain itself — what mark introduces the explanation?

quests.sentence: Their kitchen was spotless the living room was a mess
quests.correctAnswer: Their kitchen was spotless; the living room was a mess.
quests.hint: Two contrasting facts sit side by side — connect them without a conjunction.
quests.explanation: A semicolon can link two independent clauses that contrast closely with each other.

quests.sentence: Sam please send me that file when you get a chance

quests.hint: Sam is being addressed directly at the start — separate the name from the request.
quests.explanation: When a name opens a sentence as a direct address, a comma follows it before the rest of the sentence.

quests.sentence: The workers union voted to approve the new contract

quests.hint: More than one worker belongs to this union — where does the apostrophe go?
quests.explanation: For a plural noun already ending in 's,' add just an apostrophe to show possession.

quests.sentence: Pack three things for the hike water snacks and a map

quests.explanation: A colon introduces a list of items after a complete sentence.

quests.sentence: Our flight was smooth the landing was surprisingly rough

quests.hint: Two related, contrasting facts about the same trip sit side by side.
quests.explanation: A semicolon can join two independent clauses that are closely related, even when they contrast.

quests.sentence: Enjoy your trip Grandpa

quests.hint: Grandpa is being spoken to directly at the end of the sentence — separate his name with a comma.
quests.explanation: When a name used as direct address comes at the end of a sentence, a comma comes before it.

quests.sentence: The report reached one clear conclusion the marketing budget needs to double

quests.sentence: Sales dropped in the spring they rebounded strongly by summer

quests.explanation: A semicolon can join two independent clauses that are closely related in meaning.
